text:
Pontus Holmberg is the kind of forward Tampa Bay keeps finding: a sixth-round pick, a Swedish pro before he arrived, and a winger coaches trust because the other team rarely gets anything when he's out there. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile at taking chances away last season, worth 1.3 wins mostly from defense.

This season he added scoring: 6 goals and 13 points in 22 games on under 15 minutes, already more than half of last year's 22 points. Some of that is finishing above his chances, and our talent range puts his true scoring rate closer to 1.8 points per 60 than the 2.4 he's running. The last stretch shows it. After two goals against Winnipeg on Nov. 8 he's gone five games without a point, and the chances thinned out too.

The other thing worth knowing is relative: the Lightning are about five points better in expected-goal share without him at five on five, a sign his line isn't driving much right now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a real setup man last season (91st percentile in primary shot assists). Watch whether the assists return before the goal pace fades.
